text: Restless, shifting, fugitive as time itself. <break time="0.8s" /> Is a certain vast bulk of the population. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the red brick district of the lower West Side. <break time="0.8s" /> They are homeless. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet they have a hundred homes. <break time="0.8s" /> And they drift from furnished room to furnished room. <break time="0.8s" /> Transients forever. <break time="0.8s" /> In their lodging as in their hearts and minds. <break time="0.8s" /> Such houses must hold a thousand tales. <break time="0.8s" /> Most of them dull. <break time="0.8s" /> But it would be strange. <break time="0.8s" /> If no ghost could be found. <break time="0.8s" /> Among so many guests. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening after dark. <break time="0.8s" /> A young man wandered among these crumbling red mansions. <break time="0.8s" /> Ringing their bells. <break time="0.8s" /> And at the twelfth house. <break time="0.8s" /> He rested his small handbag upon the step. <break time="0.8s" /> He wiped the dust. <break time="0.8s" /> From his hatband and forehead. <break time="0.8s" /> And the bell sounded faint and far away. <break time="0.8s" /> In some remote, hollow depth of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> To the door came a housekeeper. <break time="0.8s" /> Who reminded him of an unwholesome, overfed worm. <break time="0.8s" /> And he asked her in a low voice. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether there was a room to let. <break time="0.8s" /> Come in, said the housekeeper. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose voice seemed to come. <break time="0.8s" /> From a throat lined with fur. <break time="0.8s" /> I have the third floor back. <break time="0.8s" /> Which has been vacant for a week. <break time="0.8s" /> He followed her up the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> Where a faint light softened the shadows. <break time="0.8s" /> And the carpet under his feet. <break time="0.8s" /> Had decayed until it looked like moss. <break time="0.8s" /> Growing on stone.
